tldr: Microsoft took its Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server to general availability in mid-August, giving hosted work-item, repo, and pipeline access with nothing to install — but not for Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor. By month's end, remote-hosted MCP servers had spread beyond Microsoft to AWS.
whats_new: AWS published a walkthrough wiring an AgentCore Runtime-hosted MCP server into Amazon Quick, landing the same day as a general "connect your agent to a remote MCP server" guide.
why_it_matters: Remote-hosted MCP servers are becoming the default deployment pattern over local stdio servers, but client support isn't uniform across vendors — Azure DevOps's GA release explicitly excludes Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor, so confirm compatibility before standardizing on one vendor's hosted MCP server.

status.detail: AWS and a generic how-to joined Microsoft's earlier Azure DevOps rollout, extending the shift to remotely hosted MCP servers.

track.label: Azure DevOps GA, no Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor support

beats.headline: AWS and a generic guide show remote MCP hosting spreading beyond Microsoft
beats.summary: A general how-to for connecting an agent to a remote MCP server appears the same day AWS publishes its own walkthrough wiring an AgentCore-hosted MCP server into Amazon Quick.

open_questions: Will Azure DevOps's Remote MCP Server add support for Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor, or stay Microsoft-agent-only?
Do AgentCore-hosted MCP servers interoperate with non-AWS agent clients, or is Amazon Quick similarly narrow?
take_for_builders: Before standardizing on a vendor-hosted MCP server, confirm which agent clients it actually supports — Azure DevOps's GA release explicitly locks out Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor.
